system: You are the Planner of a nonprofit-finance theory-testing pipeline. You turn a theory into a JSON test spec in the exact format shown. You choose variables, the expected sign, the unit the exposure is assigned to and controls; you never compute a statistic. The validation gate (alpha, effect floor, permutations, hold-out) is fixed by the pipeline and replaces whatever you write. Use only the column names listed. Reply with one JSON object and nothing else.
prompt:
Theory: In wealthier counties nonprofits spread their revenue over more sources instead of leaning on one.

Scout mapping: {"outcome": "revenue_concentration", "exposure": "median_household_income", "exposure_type": "continuous", "exposure_unit": "county_fips", "controls": ["log_revenue", "category", "state", "tax_year", "return_type", "nonprofit_density"], "notes": "Wealth is proxied by county median household income (continuous, county-year), and a negative association with the Herfindahl revenue_concentration index would support the theory; log_revenue, sector, state and year are the controls, and the sample should be restricted to full 990 filers."}

Example spec for a binary exposure (follow this format exactly):
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "theory_id": "ratings_fairness",
  "theory": "Standard financial-ratio ratings unfairly penalize nonprofits in high-need counties.",
  "source": "docs/ratings_theory.md",
  "written_by": "hand (CP3); from CP4 the Planner agent writes specs in this format",
  "outcome": "standard_rating",
  "exposure": "high_need",
  "expected_sign": -1,
  "exposure_unit": "county_fips",
  "exposure_varies_by": "tax_year",
  "population": {
    "return_type": ["990"],
    "require_true": ["has_county", "has_need"],
    "require_present": ["standard_rating", "high_need", "log_revenue", "category", "county_fips"]
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "The mean standard rating is lower in high-need counties than elsewhere.",
      "method": "difference_in_means"
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "claim": "The gap remains after controlling for organization size (log revenue), sector (NORP category) and tax year.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    }
  ],
  "robustness": [
    {
      "id": "H2_multilevel_2022",
      "method": "multilevel",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "categorical": ["category"],
      "group": "county_fips",
      "years": [2022]
    },
    {
      "id": "H2_county_year_means",
      "method": "two_stage_group_means",
      "controls": ["log_revenue"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category"],
      "groups": ["county_fips", "tax_year"]
    }
  ],
  "validator": {
    "alpha": 0.05,
    "effect_floor_sd": 0.1,
    "n_permutations": 999,
    "seed": 6235,
    "permutation": {"keep_paths": true, "studentized": true},
    "holdout": {"by": "state", "folds": 5},
    "holdout_year": 2022,
    "outcome_rule": {"heavy_tail_ratio": 3.0, "winsorize": [0.01, 0.99]}
  }
}


For exposure_type "continuous", set hypotheses H1.method to "correlation". Use the Scout's outcome, exposure, exposure_type and exposure_unit unchanged. Give a fresh theory_id (snake_case).
text:
{
  "spec_version": 1,
  "theory_id": "wealth_revenue_diversification",
  "theory": "In wealthier counties nonprofits spread their revenue over more sources instead of leaning on one.",
  "source": "scout mapping (CP4 Planner)",
  "written_by": "Planner agent",
  "outcome": "revenue_concentration",
  "exposure": "median_household_income",
  "expected_sign": -1,
  "exposure_unit": "county_fips",
  "exposure_varies_by": "tax_year",
  "population": {
    "return_type": ["990"],
    "require_true": ["has_county"],
    "require_present": ["revenue_concentration", "median_household_income", "log_revenue", "category", "county_fips", "state", "tax_year", "nonprofit_density"]
  },
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "id": "H1",
      "claim": "Revenue concentration (Herfindahl index) is negatively correlated with county median household income.",
      "method": "correlation"
    },
    {
      "id": "H2",
      "claim": "The negative association remains after controlling for organization size (log revenue), nonprofit density, sector (NORP category), state and tax year.",
      "method": "fixed_effects",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "nonprofit_density"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "cluster": "county_fips"
    }
  ],
  "robustness": [
    {
      "id": "H2_multilevel_2022",
      "method": "multilevel",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "nonprofit_density"],
      "categorical": ["category", "state"],
      "group": "county_fips",
      "years": [2022]
    },
    {
      "id": "H2_county_year_means",
      "method": "two_stage_group_means",
      "controls": ["log_revenue", "nonprofit_density"],
      "absorb": ["tax_year", "category", "state"],
      "groups": ["county_fips", "tax_year"]
    }
  ],
  "validator": {
    "alpha": 0.05,
    "effect_floor_sd": 0.1,
    "n_permutations": 999,
    "seed": 6235,
    "permutation": {"keep_paths": true, "studentized": true},
    "holdout": {"by": "state", "folds": 5},
    "holdout_year": 2022,
    "outcome_rule": {"heavy_tail_ratio": 3.0, "winsorize": [0.01, 0.99]}
  }
}
